verdict.rationale: Jitsu Functions run automatically on every incoming event and can filter, transform, and enrich it in JavaScript/TypeScript. Their Fetch API can make HTTP requests to third-party services, so code-defined conditional logic can trigger outbound actions per event. The webhook destination can also forward events to any HTTP endpoint. However, Functions are positioned as a data-processing step before delivery rather than a rule/automation engine, and there is no documented declarative rule builder or catalog of trigger→action types. The built-in Email/Slack notifications only cover sync and batch failures and are not user-defined rules. missing for 10: declarative rule definition (no-code conditions→actions), documented automation/workflow examples beyond data transformation, a range of action types beyond HTTP calls, independent hands-on corroboration of event-triggered actions.
